pages.title: 0 2 11 Recovery and Shop Candidate Register
pages.intro: IMPLEMENTED_CANDIDATE 0.2.11 / code 14; FinalVerification passed 204 EditMode and 144 PlayMode, all 12 Editor captures reviewed, Quest/PICO APKs built and audited. Worn-headset usability and performance acceptance pending.

blocks.text: Historical 0.2.10 / code 13 passed 184 EditMode and 115 PlayMode and built both APKs. Those reports, screenshots, installation and user feedback do not validate 0.2.11.

GD-WATER-10/11: explicit TickRecovery after the accepted simulation step; 3 eligible seconds then 0.25 units/second, capacity-clamped with fractional carry. RecoveryWaiting and RecoveryActive control the gauge cue. RecoveredWater is separate from SuppliedWater and ConsumedWater and is restored with all tank amounts at retry.

The root supplies focused/settled/tracked fireground eligibility and raw trigger-held state. Shop, navigation, modal, loading, pause, tracking loss, manual refill and weapon operation restart the delay. Tool switches, successful purchases/upgrades, source disconnect and sector transitions grant no immediate water.

New recovery rule and root-interaction tests are authored. The old no-regeneration test now verifies that ordinary simulation Tick cannot guess recovery eligibility or double-credit the explicit transaction. FinalVerification passed 204 EditMode and 144 PlayMode with zero failed, skipped or inconclusive. This includes 20 new EditMode and 26 new PlayMode cases plus 3 restored existing PlayMode cases; restored coverage is not newly authored. All 12 final Editor captures were reviewed; APK audits passed and are recorded in ReleaseEvidence.json.

GD-SHOP-01/02 and AR-SHOP-01: Equipment, Tuning and Station pages implement tool/tune/station catalogue identities, same-model numeric comparisons, highlighted station control results, explicit fallback, separate purchase and current/result comparison. The preview copies renderer data only, with no physics/audio/particles/gameplay components and one same-key-cached active geometry object. Optional thumbnails, rotate/demo and render textures are not implemented. Catalogue and layout tests passed within FinalVerification; device stereo/performance acceptance is pending.

Intermediate verification is not release acceptance. InitialVerification passed 204 EditMode; PlayMode ran 132 with 62 passed and 70 failed because the new preview constructed MaterialPropertyBlock in a MonoBehaviour field initializer. Lazy creation in Show corrects that failure. Import audit also found invalid 33-character GUIDs on the new preview test group and two existing groups (outlet feedback and station shop), so those tests had not compiled. All three metadata IDs were normalized after checking references and force-reimported. The subsequent ReleaseVerification passed the complete compiled suite of 204 EditMode and 143 PlayMode; 3 restored existing cases must not be presented as newly written tests.

Twelve final Editor synthetic captures were reviewed after increasing preview size, shortening the numeric-tuning description, lowering the price row and correcting SPEED to actual world metres per second. They show waiting/active recovery, all four tools, numeric tuning before/after purchase, rotary result, current lever, button result and seated/standing shop placement. The second station comparison and purchase use public scene APIs to avoid same-frame UI debounce; these captures do not prove every flow was completed with live headset input. FinalVerification includes the additional text-layout regression and passed 204 EditMode and 144 PlayMode.

Quest and PICO APKs passed version 0.2.11/code 14, ARM64, signature/icon, exact Camp/Fireground scene whitelist and settings-restoration audits. Both builds report zero errors, with 8 Quest warnings and 12 PICO warnings. Source integrity is recorded in Logs/EmberdeepRecoveryShop/ReleaseEvidence.json; these build checks do not establish headset operation or performance. Quest 3 replacement installation and app info verified 0.2.11/code 14. The device was Asleep and no app process was observed; physical hand tracking, comfort, stereo readability and performance remain pending. No PICO hardware acceptance is claimed.

pages.title: Historical M1 Decisions and Subsequent Overrides
pages.intro: Historical 0.2.0/0.2.1 decisions are retained below. The subsequent 0.2.3 system hand pointer remains; 0.2.5 replaces the initial hydrant with a lever well and removes rotary tap fallback. InteractionIntentFix.json defines current placement and interaction work; M2/M3 remain proposed.

blocks.text: Accessible valve

Historical 0.2.0 M1-DD-01 implemented a fresh broad-valve pinch and release with at most five degrees of rotation as an accessible detent toggle. A normal 45-degree turn also works. Larger incomplete turns retain the previous detent. Both paths use the same flow duration, tank clamp and interruption rules.
Retry and UI ownership

M1-DD-02 restores the current sector entry tanks, supply counters and attempt earnings on Retry. New Expedition is a separate camp operation. M1-DD-03 routes fireground buttons through the existing gaze-and-fresh-pinch recognizer; parallel native SDK callbacks are removed from these buttons. Existing hand data and pinch filtering remain shared. M1-DD-04 also reuses the repaired 0.35-second stable acquisition and raw-head validation for fireground first placement and explicit recenter, with no timeout fallback; headset placement acceptance remains pending.
Replaceable blockout assets

WS-01 hydrant, WS-02 creek intake and WS-03 refill pump are scale-one procedural blockouts. Public Socket, Valve, Pump, Intake and IntakeSocket anchors define the interaction interface. Equipment exposes RefillPort. Gauges, flow lamps, source hoses and broad cyan handles provide state feedback. Decorative colliders are disabled. Production meshes, animation, material/shader completion, budgets and both-eye approval remain outstanding.
Acceptance boundary

Historical 0.2.0 acceptance: the user confirmed front placement of the repaired menu only, not all buttons, devices or hand tracking. No device performance or comfort claim was made. The newer interaction failure and candidate below supersede the earlier availability statement.
Historical 0.2.1 index-ray implementation

On 2026-11-08, user feedback reported hand-tracked buttons unusable and explicitly required index-finger ray pointing with same-hand pinch. This replaces the head-gaze selection part of M1-DD-03 across camp, settings, quit confirmation, fireground HUD and shop. Stable head-pose menu placement remains. EmberdeepHandRay derives the ray from existing tracked index joints and preserves its open origin and direction in palm space during pinch curl. EmberdeepHandRayMenu displays a thin cyan ray/cursor and permits only the pointing hand's fresh pinch. It reuses the shared tracked-hand provider and pinch filter.

Both hands, different simultaneous targets, wrong-hand pinch, tracking recovery, nonfinite samples, page ownership, pause/focus, actual shop purchase and HUD cannon cancellation have synthetic rule or PlayMode regressions. Historical 0.2.1/code 4 passed 129 EditMode and 30 PlayMode tests with zero failures under Logs/EmberdeepV2/ReleaseVerification. The historical 119/17 results validate only 0.2.0. ArtV2Iteration.json records the separate new model and rendering delivery. APK audits are tracked in Logs/EmberdeepV2/ReleaseEvidence.json. No headset was connected in that historical iteration; repeat M1DeviceAcceptance.json on PICO 4 and Quest 3. All three English DOCX are regenerated with structural content QA; that iteration's visual rendering remained unavailable and is not claimed.

water_recovery.api: FireRun.TickRecovery(dt, eligible, triggerActive), ResetRecovery(), RecoveredWater, RecoveryWaiting, RecoveryActive and RecoveryDelayRemaining. FireRescueGame.ProcessWaterRecovery applies the live scene gates.
water_recovery.clock: Exactly one explicit transaction after the accepted simulation step. Accept finite positive dt up to 0.1 seconds per call; discard excess rather than banking it. Delay uses eligible active time only; crossing frames credit only the part after the delay. Preserve fractional water and sub-float rounding carry.
water_recovery.gates: Fighting/Cleared, owned active loadout, focused settled fireground, valid tracking, positive timeScale, no Shop/modal/navigation/placement transition, no manual-source lock, pending dock, empty-outlet action, active cannon pump, raw held trigger, charge or firing. A racked equipped owned loadout may recover; a selected preview cannot.
water_recovery.transactions: Successful equip/purchase/tuning/station upgrade, source connection/disconnection, stage/outcome transition, retry and external suspension reset the delay. Recovery changes only the active tank and RecoveredWater; the sector checkpoint restores tanks, supplied/recovered/consumed counters, equipment ownership/upgrades, station tier and economy together.
water_recovery.feedback: Quiet droplet with RECOVERY Waiting or SLOW RECOVERY +0.25/s beside the gauge; hidden when ineligible or full. Empty active recovery offers the pump as the faster alternative. No recovery sound, haptic, hand ownership or world water emitter.
